name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single large, high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. It must be visible at all times, not just on focus, so keyboard users see it immediately without tabbing. This solves the "where do I start?" problem for assistive tech users while keeping the interface clean for others. The trade-off is a small permanent visual element, but it’s worth the clarity it brings to navigation.

name: Reader
text: The risk: A permanently visible skip link at full size blocks sighted keyboard users from the main content until they tab past it, creating a new barrier. Better: Hide it off-screen until focus arrives, then animate it into view—this keeps it discoverable for keyboard users without cluttering the page for others. Settle it with a quick user test: time how long it takes sighted keyboard users to reach the main content with both approaches.
